module.Chapter: Chapter 5 · Functions, Files, and Raspberry Pi
module.Title: Build a Start-Permissive Function
module.Teaching: A function can return a Boolean expression directly, making safety rules reusable and testable.
module.ExampleCode:
def valve_can_open(command, interlock):
    return command and not interlock
module.TargetCode:
def can_start(door_closed, emergency_stop):
    return door_closed and not emergency_stop
module.FillStarter:
def can_start(___, ___):
    return door_closed and ___ emergency_stop
module.PredictionExplanation: The and/not expression evaluates to True or False.
module.BrokenCode:
def can_start(door_closed, emergency_stop):
    print door_closed and emergency_stop
module.DebugPrompt: Return the safe Boolean expression and reverse the emergency-stop condition.
module.RecallPrompt: Rebuild can_start from memory. Use these exact identifiers: door_closed, emergency_stop.
module.TransferPrompt: Create can_run_pump(level_ok, overload) returning the safe permissive.
module.TransferCode:
def can_run_pump(level_ok, overload):
    return level_ok and not overload
module.PreviewMessage: Equipment permissives can now be reused throughout the program.
